C Preprocessor Directives: `#include <file.h>` searches system headers, `#include "file.h"` searches local directory first. `#define MACRO(x) ((x) * (x))` performs text substitution (always parenthesize arguments to avoid precedence bugs). Conditional compilation uses `#ifdef`, `#ifndef`, `#if defined()`, `#else`, `#elif`, and `#endif` to prevent multiple inclusions via header guards.

Macro Stringification and Concatenation: The `#` operator turns a macro argument into a string literal (e.g., `#define STR(x) #x`). The `##` operator concatenates two tokens together (e.g., `#define CONCAT(a, b) a ## b`). `#undef MACRO` undefines a macro.

Data Types & Sizes: Standard types include `char` (at least 8 bits/1 byte), `short` (at least 16 bits), `int` (native integer size, at least 16 bits, usually 32 bits), `long` (at least 32 bits), `long long` (at least 64 bits), `float` (single precision floating point), `double` (double precision), `long double` (extended precision). Qualifiers: `signed` and `unsigned` affect bit interpretation.

Storage Classes & Scope: `auto` (default local variables allocated on stack), `register` (hints compiler to store variable in CPU register; cannot take address using `&`), `static` (local variables retain state between function calls; global static variables/functions restrict visibility/linkage strictly to the current translation unit/file), `extern` (declares a variable defined in another file/scope without allocating memory).

Type Qualifiers & Enumerations: `const` makes a variable read-only. `volatile` informs the compiler that a variable's value may change externally (disables compiler optimizations/caching in registers). `enum boolean { FALSE, TRUE };` assigns integer constants starting from 0 unless explicitly set (e.g., `enum flags { FOO = 1, BAR = 4 };`).

Bitwise Operators: Bitwise AND `&`, OR `|`, XOR `^`, One's Complement (NOT) `~`, Left Shift `<<` (multiplies by 2^n), Right Shift `>>` (divides by 2^n; implementation-dependent signed shift). Masking example: `x = x & ~077` clears the low-order 6 bits of `x`.

Operator Precedence & Evaluation Order: Highest to lowest: 1. `() [] -> .` 2. Unary `! ~ ++ -- + - * & (type) sizeof` (right-to-left) 3. Arithmetic `* / %` then `+ -` 4. Bitwise shifts `<< >>` 5. Relational `< <= > >=` then `== !=` 6. Bitwise `&`, `^`, `|` 7. Logical `&&`, `||` 8. Conditional `?:` 9. Assignment `= += -=` etc. (right-to-left) 10. Comma `,`. Note: Sequence points guarantee evaluation order only for `&&`, `||`, `?:`, and `,`.

Control Flow Constructs: `switch(expression)` requires integer/char constants in `case` labels. Statements fall through unless interrupted by `break`. `default:` handles unmatched cases. `do { ... } while(condition);` guarantees at least one execution pass. `goto label;` jumps unconditionally within the same function scope.

Pointers and Addresses: `&p` fetches memory address of `p`. `*p` dereferences pointer `p` to access underlying value. Null pointer `NULL` is guaranteed to point to invalid memory (typically physical address 0). Indirection through an uninitialized pointer leads to Undefined Behavior (segmentation fault).

Pointer Arithmetic & Arrays: Array name `a[i]` is equivalent to `*(a + i)`. Adding integer `n` to pointer `p` increments address by `n * sizeof(*p)` bytes. Subtracting two pointers of the same array yields the number of elements between them (`ptrdiff_t`). Valid pointer operations: assignment of same type, addition/subtraction of pointer and integer, pointer subtraction, comparison (`==`, `!=`, `<`, `>`), and comparing to `NULL` or 0.

String Constants & Character Pointers: `char pm[] = "hello";` creates a mutable array of characters on the stack. `char *pm = "hello";` creates a pointer to a read-only string literal stored in static memory; modifying `*pm` causes undefined behavior.

Pointers to Pointers & Function Pointers: Function pointers allow passing behavior as data: `int (*comp)(const void *, const void *)`. Declaration syntax: `int *f()` is a function returning an int pointer, whereas `int (*f)()` is a pointer to a function returning an int.

Structures (`struct`): Group heterogeneous variables in contiguous memory. Access fields via `structure.member` or pointer `structure_ptr->member` (equivalent to `(*structure_ptr).member`). Structs can be assigned, passed to functions, and returned by value. Memory alignment padding may insert unused bytes between members to align with machine word boundaries.

Unions & Bit-fields: `union` allocates memory sufficient only for its largest member, sharing the exact same memory space among all members (only one member valid at a time). Bit-fields allow pack structures into specific bit-widths inside unsigned integers: `struct flags { unsigned int is_active : 1; unsigned int mode : 3; };`.
Typedef: Creates new data type aliases: `typedef char *String;`. `typedef struct Node { int data; struct Node *next; } Node;` enables self-referential structures (linked lists, trees).

Standard I/O (<stdio.h>): `FILE *fp = fopen(filename, mode);` Modes: `"r"` (read), `"w"` (write/truncate), `"a"` (append), `"rb"`/`"wb"` (binary mode). Returns `NULL` on failure. `fclose(fp)` flushes buffers and closes file stream. Predefined streams: `stdin`, `stdout`, `stderr`.

Formatted I/O Signatures: `printf("format", ...)` writes to `stdout`. `fprintf(fp, ...)` writes to file stream. `sprintf(buffer, ...)` writes to char array. `snprintf(buf, size, ...)` prevents buffer overflows. Specifiers: `%d` (int), `%ld` (long), `%f` (double), `%c` (char), `%s` (string), `%p` (pointer address), `%x` (hexadecimal), `%%` (literal %). `scanf` reads input using pointers: `scanf("%d", &var);`.

Character and Block I/O: `int fgetc(FILE *fp)` / `int fputc(int c, FILE *fp)` read/write individual characters, returning `EOF` (-1) on end-of-file or error. `char *fgets(char *buf, int n, FILE *fp)` reads up to `n-1` characters stopping at newlines. `size_t fread(void *ptr, size_t size, size_t nmemb, FILE *fp)` and `fwrite` handle raw binary execution blocks.

Dynamic Memory Allocation (<stdlib.h>): `void *malloc(size_t size)` allocates `size` uninitialized bytes on the heap. `void *calloc(size_t num, size_t size)` allocates zero-initialized memory. `void *realloc(void *ptr, size_t new_size)` resizes allocated memory block (may move block location). Always check if return value is `NULL`. Free dynamically allocated memory using `free(ptr);` to prevent memory leaks. Re-using freed memory leads to 'use-after-free' bugs.

UNIX Low-Level File I/O: Operates via integer file descriptors (`0`: stdin, `1`: stdout, `2`: stderr). System calls: `int open(char *name, int flags, int mode)` (flags: `O_RDONLY`, `O_WRONLY`, `O_RDWR`), `int creat(char *name, int mode)`. Read/Write: `int read(int fd, char *buf, int n)`, `int write(int fd, char *buf, int n)`. Repositioning stream offset: `long lseek(int fd, long offset, int origin)` where `origin`: 0 (beginning), 1 (current), 2 (end).
